record.paper_title: Global results on rational systems in the plane, part 1
record.original_question: Among the group of 300 non-single-equation special cases of the nonnegative-parameter planar rational system x_{n+1} = (a1 + b1 x_n + g1 y_n)/(A1 + B1 x_n + C1 y_n), y_{n+1} = (a2 + b2 x_n + g2 y_n)/(A2 + B2 x_n + C2 y_n), with nonnegative initial conditions and positive denominators, 188 systems are neither competitive nor cooperative in any parameter region. For each of these 188 systems, determine the global character of its solutions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the planar rational system of first-order difference equations

  x_{n+1} = (a_1 + b_1 x_n + g_1 y_n)/(A_1 + B_1 x_n + C_1 y_n),
  y_{n+1} = (a_2 + b_2 x_n + g_2 y_n)/(A_2 + B_2 x_n + C_2 y_n),

for n = 0, 1, 2, ..., where all twelve parameters a_i, b_i, g_i, A_i, B_i, C_i (i = 1, 2) are nonnegative real numbers, the initial condition (x_0, y_0) is in [0,∞)^2, and at every iterate the denominators A_1 + B_1 x_n + C_1 y_n and A_2 + B_2 x_n + C_2 y_n are strictly positive. By normalization, one reduces to those parameter choices in which each numerator and denominator contains a nonzero subset of its three possible terms; excluding cases that degenerate into a single first-order rational equation, this produces a list of 300 distinct nontrivial special cases.

A planar map F = (F_1, F_2) acting on a subset of [0,∞)^2 is called competitive on an invariant region if F_1 is nondecreasing in x and nonincreasing in y while F_2 is nonincreasing in x and nondecreasing in y, and cooperative if both components are nondecreasing in each variable. Within the list of 300 systems above, exactly 188 of them have the property that, for every choice of admissible nonnegative parameters making the system nondegenerate, the associated map is neither competitive nor cooperative on any invariant subregion of the nonnegative quadrant.

Problem: For each of these 188 systems, determine the global character of its nonnegative solutions. That is, classify (in terms of the parameters) all equilibria and periodic points, their local and global stability, the basins of attraction, the existence of invariant manifolds, and the asymptotic behavior as n → ∞ of every solution starting from a nonnegative initial condition with positive denominators.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open research program calling for a case-by-case global analysis of 188 specific planar rational systems that are neither competitive nor cooperative. Individual subcases have been studied in subsequent literature on rational planar systems, but no comprehensive resolution of all 188 systems appears to have been published, and the problem is generally still treated as open.
